metadata.services: Triple Play Bundle: Fiber 500 + Digital TV + Voice ($110/mo)

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is David. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi David. I'm having a lot of trouble with my cell service. My calls keep dropping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very sorry to hear that. I know how frustrating that can be. I can definitely look into that for you. To get started, can I get your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thomas Taylor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Taylor. And can you confirm the phone number you're calling about?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. I'm pulling up your account now. For security purposes, to access the account details, could you please provide me with your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Uh, yeah, hold on. I think it's... 5141.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's correct. Thank you for verifying your information, Mr. Taylor.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I see you have our Triple Play Bundle with Fiber internet. Now, you mentioned you're experiencing dropped calls. Can you tell me a little more about when and where this happens?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's mainly in my house. Specifically, I have a home office set up in my basement, and almost every single call I make or receive down there drops within a minute or two. It's impossible to get any work done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand completely. That must be incredibly disruptive, especially for a home office. Is this a new problem, or has it been happening for a while?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's always been a bit spotty in the basement, but it seems to have gotten much worse over the last couple of weeks. I don't get it. I have your internet service too, and the Wi-Fi is great down there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very helpful piece of information. And just to be thorough, does this happen anywhere else in your house, or primarily just the basement?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Mostly the basement. Upstairs is... okay. Sometimes it cuts out for a second near the kitchen, but it's the basement office that's the real problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. Thank you for that detail. What I'd like to do first is check the signal strength and tower performance in your area from my end. This will just take me about 30 to 40 seconds. Is it okay if I put you on a brief hold?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, that's fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll be right back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Taylor.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No problem. Find anything?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Looking at our network map, the cellular tower that services your address is operating perfectly, with no reported issues. The signal strength in your neighborhood is generally strong.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So... why are my calls dropping?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great question. Often, even with a strong outdoor signal, materials in a home's construction—like concrete, rebar, or certain types of insulation—can weaken or block the signal. This is especially common in basements, which are below ground level. It's a phenomenon called signal attenuation.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So I'm just stuck with no service in my office?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all. We have a great solution for this exact situation. You mentioned your Cymbal Wi-Fi signal is strong in the basement, correct?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, the Wi-Fi is perfect. I get full bars on my laptop and phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. In that case, we can enable a feature on your phone called Wi-Fi Calling. It allows your phone to make and receive calls and texts over your Wi-Fi network instead of the cellular network whenever your cell signal is weak.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh. I think I've heard of that. Does that cost extra?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very common question. No, there is no extra charge for it. It's a standard feature included with your Cymbal Telecom mobile plan. Let me just double-check your account to ensure it's enabled on our end.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just one moment... yes, I can confirm the feature is available and ready to be activated on your line. We just need to turn it on within your phone's settings.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Alright. How do we do that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can walk you through it right now. What kind of phone do you have? Is it an iPhone or an Android?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's an iPhone. A 13, I think.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. iPhones make it very straightforward. Are you able to go into your phone's settings while we're on this call?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yeah, I can do that. Okay, I'm on the main Settings screen now. I see Airplane Mode, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please scroll down a little bit and tap on 'Phone'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, tapped 'Phone'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. In that menu, you should see an option that says 'Wi-Fi Calling'. Do you see it?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let's see... yep, I see it. It says 'Off' next to it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's what we want to change. Please tap on 'Wi-Fi Calling'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now you should see a toggle switch at the top that says 'Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone'. Please tap that switch to turn it on.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Alright, I tapped it. A pop-up just appeared. It says 'Enable Wi-Fi Calling?'

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, go ahead and tap the 'Enable' button.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... now it's loading a new screen. 'Emergency Address'. It wants me to confirm my address for 911 calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, this is a very important step. Because you're using your internet connection, 911 services need to know your physical location in case of an emergency. Is the address shown on the screen your correct home address?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it is. It looks correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please go ahead and confirm that address.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I hit 'Confirm Address'. It says 'Wi-Fi Calling is now on'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic. That's exactly what we wanted to see. Now, for the final confirmation, please look at the very top left corner of your iPhone's screen, where the carrier name is usually displayed.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I'm looking...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does it still say 'Cymbal', or has it changed?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Whoa. It now says 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'. I've never seen that before.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's perfect. That's the visual confirmation that your phone is now routing calls through your Wi-Fi network. This should completely solve the issue of dropped calls in your basement office.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Really? That's it? That seems... too easy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a powerful feature, and often the simplest solution is the best one. Now, I want to be 100% certain this has resolved your problem. The best way to test it is to try a call.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, what do you want me to do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In a moment, I'm going to ask you to hang up this call. I will then immediately call you right back on this same number. Since you're in your basement, if the call connects and you can hear me clearly, it will be proof that Wi-Fi Calling is working as it should.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. We hang up, you call me back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. Before we do that, do you have any other questions for me about this or anything else with your account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, not right now. Let's just see if this works first.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sounds like a plan. I will be calling you back in approximately 10 seconds after we disconnect. Ready?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Ready. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. Talk to you in a moment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Taylor, this is David from Cymbal Telecom calling you back. How is the call quality now?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wow. It's... it's perfect. It's crystal clear. I can't believe it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am so glad to hear that! This confirms that your phone is now using your Wi-Fi for the call, bypassing the weak cellular signal in the basement.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is a game changer. I've been struggling with this for weeks. Why didn't I know about this?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's one of those features that you don't know you need until you do. We try to message it, but it's easy to miss. I'm just happy we were able to get it working for you today.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So, just to be clear, anytime I'm at home on my Wi-Fi, my phone will use this automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. Your phone is smart enough to know when to use it. If you have a weak cellular signal but a strong Wi-Fi connection, it will automatically switch to Wi-Fi Calling. When you leave the house and your Wi-Fi, it will seamlessly switch back to the cellular network.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And it works for incoming calls too? People can call me and it will just work?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. It works for both incoming and outgoing calls, as well as text messages.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's fantastic. David, you've saved my workday. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is my absolute pleasure, Mr. Taylor. I'm really glad we could find a simple and effective solution for you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So is there anything else I need to do? Or is that it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's it. You are all set. The setting will remain on unless you manually turn it off in the future.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I won't be doing that. This is great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm happy to hear it. I've also added a note to your account detailing the issue and the resolution by enabling Wi-Fi Calling, so if you ever call back, the next agent will know exactly what was done.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Excellent. Thank you for being so thorough.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, it's part of our commitment to service at Cymbal Telecom.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I have one more quick question, if you don't mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all, I'm here to help. What's on your mind?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Does this work on other Wi-Fi networks? Like if I'm at a coffee shop or the airport?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an excellent question. Yes, it does. As long as you are connected to a stable Wi-Fi network, anywhere in the world, Wi-Fi Calling can work. It's a great way to avoid roaming charges when you're traveling internationally, too.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wow, okay. I did not know that. That's a really good tip.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a very useful feature to keep in mind for travel. Just remember that some public Wi-Fi networks, like at hotels, may have firewalls that could block it, but generally, it works very well.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Good to know. I'll keep that in mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Was there anything else I could assist you with today, Mr. Taylor? Perhaps any questions about your bill or other services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, I think that's all. You've solved my main problem, and that's all I was hoping for today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. Well, I'm very happy we could get this sorted out for you. I'll let you get back to your day and enjoy your crystal-clear calls.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thanks again, David. I really appreciate your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are most welcome. Thank you for being a valued Cymbal Telecom customer, and have a great rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just making some final notes on the account... Let's add detail on the troubleshooting steps.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Confirmed customer location and signal attenuation in basement. Explained Wi-Fi calling.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Guided customer through enabling Wi-Fi calling on iPhone 13.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Confirmed Emergency 911 address update.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Verified successful activation by checking carrier string 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Performed successful test call to customer's device while in the problem area.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Customer confirmed clear call quality and expressed satisfaction with the resolution.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also provided additional information on using Wi-Fi calling on other networks and for international travel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Customer had no further questions.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Account notes are complete. Setting resolution code to 'Technical Support > Mobile > Wi-Fi Calling Enabled'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Call disposition finalized.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, ready for the next call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's review the quality checklist for that last interaction.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Greeting was standard. Verification was correct. Empathy was shown.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Troubleshooting steps were logical and clearly communicated.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Resolution was confirmed with a test, which is key.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Offered further assistance and provided a proper closing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I believe that meets all the quality standards.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Time to mark myself as available.
